name: Predestination versus free will and works
plain_explanation: Protestants, following the part of Saint Augustine's theology that concerns the soul's fate, taught that whether a soul is saved or damned is fixed by God in advance (predestination), regardless of a priest's or the individual's own actions. The Jesuits taught the opposite: humans have genuine free will, and salvation comes from both faith and good works, not faith alone.
precise_definition: Predestination: the doctrine that God has eternally and unconditionally determined the salvation or damnation of each soul, independent of the actions of priests or, in the strict Calvinist form, of the individual's own deeds. The Jesuit counter-doctrine held that free will is real and that salvation requires both faith and works, directly rejecting the Augustinian strand the Reformers emphasized.
why_it_mattered: It reshaped the practical power of the clergy: if salvation does not depend on priestly intervention (masses, indulgences), the Church's economic and spiritual hold over believers weakens, which is why Russell treats predestination as politically as much as theologically significant.
historical_origin: Rooted in Saint Augustine's theology, revived selectively by Luther and Calvin in the sixteenth century and rejected by the Jesuits at and after the Council of Trent.
examples: The abolition of purgatory and the rejection of Indulgences, both of which had depended on the idea that priestly/papal action could affect a soul's fate
objections: The Jesuit position that predestination is false and that free will and works matter
competing_positions: The Jesuit doctrine of free will and salvation by faith and works
influence_on_later_thinkers: The dispute over free will and predestination recurs later in the book's treatment of Hobbes's determinism and of theological controversies surrounding Descartes and his contemporaries.
connection_to_politics_or_religion: Directly religious in origin but with immediate political consequences for clerical power, discussed below.
